analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour + ASML / BCP / BNP / RIO 14 Oct 2026
key_insights: US equities closed lower Tuesday: SPX -2bps to 7805 (6 of 11 sectors down, Healthcare -1.33%, Financials -0.41%, Energy +1.74%), NDX -31bps to 30,569 (semis down a fifth straight day, memory -4%), RTY -40bps to 2783. The GS Cyclicals vs Defensives pair traded lower on 6 of 7 sessions.
Q3 bank earnings were mixed. JPM -86bps after missing on profit and revenue but guiding NII positively. WFC -3.1% after an EPS beat and revenue miss. C -5.6% on cautious commentary.
In Europe, semis (GSSBSEMI -3.7%) followed Asia lower (KOSPI -5.5%, NKY -1.8%), while Value (GSPEVALU +90bps) and Size (GSP3SIZE +40bps) outperformed.

Wells Fargo said wages and employment are strong and keeping pace with inflation. Debit card spending was +8% and credit card spending +12% y/y, broad-based across categories. Charge-offs are below the prior quarter and prior year, and early-stage delinquencies are at historically low levels. Lower-income households stay sensitive to financing costs, while high-income households benefit from strong asset prices and stable labor income.

GS CPI preview: September core CPI +0.24% m/m (consensus +0.2%), +2.46% y/y (consensus +2.5%). Headline CPI +0.59% m/m (consensus +0.6%), driven by higher energy prices. The forecast is consistent with a slightly smaller 0.20% rise in September core PCE.

GS desk corporate buyback activity was light last week as companies sat in pre-earnings blackout. Flows were 0.8x 2025 YTD ADTV and 0.8x 2024 YTD ADTV, in line with the prior week, concentrated in Financials, Health Care and Energy.

CTA positioning in US equities sits at the 27th percentile on a 1-year lookback and the 54th on a 5-year lookback. CTAs have sold heavily in Russell stocks and are the shortest in the index since 2023.
US L/S gross leverage rose 3.8 pts to 213% (53rd percentile, 1-year). US L/S net leverage rose 0.5 pts to 46.9% (2nd percentile, 1-year), the first increase in four weeks.
October is the fiscal year-end for about $2.306 trillion of active fund assets (678 funds) and $1.736 trillion of passive fund assets (81 funds).
GS estimates AI demand is adding about 45bp to core PCE inflation, roughly half of it genuine and half mismeasurement. The effect is expected to peak at 50bp by end-2026 and fall to 10bp by end-2027.

ASML beat and raised. Q3 gross margin was 57.4%, before recent price increases, and Q4 gross margin is guided to 57%. The company said 30% growth in 2027 and 2028 will not meet customer demand and it is looking at ways to extend capacity further, especially in 2028 and beyond.
ASML previously guided FY27 low-NA EUV capacity to about 85 tools (buy-side nearer 90), with potential capacity above 110 tools by 2028. AMAT disappointed on its gross margin guide the day before.
Banco Comercial Português (BCP) upgraded to Buy with a EUR1.35 price target (20% upside), using recent weakness as an entry point. GS estimates are 2%/5%/5% above consensus for 2026/27/28.

BNP Q3 preview: GS models net profit before AT1 of about EUR3.4bn, 3% above Visible Alpha consensus. Revenue is about EUR350mn (3%) above consensus, mainly from CIB and Retail. This is partly offset by a tax charge about EUR200mn above consensus (about 30% effective rate due to an exceptional item BNP guided to). Opex and provisions are in line with the Street. Price target EUR136 (50% upside), 2026E EPS cut 3%.

Rio Tinto Q3: production and cost guidance unchanged, iron ore in line, nothing on CMRG. Copper was 2% below consensus. Bingham base effects and a concentrator rebuild that consensus did not adjust for explain the miss. Oyu Tolgoi was 17% above consensus. Escondida was 5% below, with September output seen back at 100kt (-15.6% y/y). Chile remains weak and copper supply stays impaired.

market_movers.rationale: Banco Comercial Português upgraded to Buy on recent weakness, with GS estimates 2%/5%/5% above consensus for 2026/27/28 and growth potential not reflected in consensus or valuation.
BNP Paribas preview: GS models net profit about 3% above consensus on top-line outperformance, partly offset by a higher tax charge. Price target implies 50% upside.
Q3 beat and raise with gross margin of 57.4% before price increases. Management is looking to extend capacity beyond the 2027 and 2028 plans.
Q3 guidance unchanged. Copper was 2% below consensus, offset in part by Oyu Tolgoi 17% above, while Escondida was 5% below.

sector_views.rationale: Semis fell a fifth straight day in the US (memory -4%) and fell in Europe following Asia, while ASML's capacity commentary points to strong demand.
Big-bank Q3 results were mixed, with several stocks falling despite beats. Wells Fargo described the consumer as strong.
Copper supply remains impaired, with Chile weak and Escondida output down 15.6% y/y in September.

earnings_insights: JPM Q3 (reported, Oct 14): missed on profit and revenue versus consensus, with positive NII guidance. Stock -86bps.
WFC Q3 (reported, Oct 14): EPS beat, revenue miss versus consensus. Stock -3.1%.
C Q3 (reported, Oct 14): stock -5.6% after cautious commentary.
ASML Q3 (reported): beat and raise. Gross margin 57.4% reported, before the recent price increases. Q4 gross margin guided to 57%.
BNP Q3 preview (GS estimate, not yet reported): net profit before AT1 about EUR3.4bn, 3% above Visible Alpha consensus. Revenue about EUR350mn above consensus. Effective tax rate about 30%.
Rio Tinto Q3 operational update (reported 13 Oct): copper 2% below consensus, Oyu Tolgoi 17% above consensus, Escondida 5% below consensus. Production and cost guidance unchanged.
AMAT (reported 13 Oct): disappointed on gross margin guidance, per this note.
